citations.quote: The primary endpoint of the study was time to platelet response, defined by platelet count \ge 150,000/\mu\text{L} and cessation of daily plasma exchange within 5 days of satisfying the platelet threshold.

A total of 145 patients were enrolled in the HERCULES study; the median age was 45 (range: 18 to 79) years, 69% were female, 73% were White. Patients were randomized to either CABLIVI (n=72) or placebo (n=73).

result.text: Time to platelet response favored caplacizumab: HR 1.58 (95% CI 1.11, 2.24), log-rank p=0.0099. target_moa.text: Caplacizumab is a bivalent humanized anti-vWF antibody fragment that binds the A1 domain of von Willebrand Factor and inhibits the interaction between vWF and platelets, thereby reducing vWF-mediated platelet adhesion and formation of microthrombi.

citations.quote: Caplacizumab is a monoclonal antibody that binds to the A1 domain of vWF and inhibits the interaction between vWF and platelets.

Caplacizumab appears to bind to the A1-domain of von Willebrand Factor (vWF) and inhibits the interaction between vWF and platelets thereby reducing vWF-mediated platelet adhesion and formation of microthrombi.

Caplacizumab (Cablivi®) is a new molecular entity (NME). Caplacizumab is an injectable (intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous (SC)) humanized bivalent anti-von Willebrand Factor (vWF) antibody fragment that consists of two identical building blocks, genetically linked by a three-alanine linker.

key_safety.text: Most frequent adverse reactions (>15%) were epistaxis, headache, and gingival bleeding (gingival bleeding 16% vs 3% placebo; fatigue 15% vs 9%). Bleeding events occurred in ~58% on CABLIVI vs 43% on placebo; serious bleeding reactions in ≥2% included epistaxis (4%) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (2%).
